Summary: Attendance Session Management
Description: Create and maintain attendance sessions aligned to valid timetable slots with a resolved eligible roster. Satisfies FR-01, FR-02, FR-03, FR-05 and the timetable/duplicate rules in DDD section 11.

Summary: Create an attendance session from a timetable slot
Description: As a Faculty member, I want to create an attendance session for a timetable slot I teach, so that a governed session with a resolved roster exists before I mark attendance.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am authenticated Faculty within my assignment scope (or an Academic Admin), When I POST /api/v1/academics/attendance/sessions with batchId, subjectId, timetableEntryId, attendanceDate and periodNo, Then a session is persisted with status OPEN and the eligible roster resolved into rosterCount, an AttendanceSessionCreated event is written to the outbox, and the response returns sessionId, status, rosterCount, requestId and correlationId (FR-01, FR-03, DDD sections 19 and 23). NOTE: the representative event in DDD Appendix E shows data.status ACTIVE, which is not a state in the section 13 lifecycle (DRAFT, OPEN, SUBMITTED, LOCKED, CORRECTED, ARCHIVED, CANCELLED); align the event sample with the lifecycle.

Summary: Validate the timetable slot and fail closed when the timetable is unavailable
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want to validate every new session against the effective published timetable from ACD-05, so that attendance can only exist for a real scheduled slot.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a session request, When timetableEntryId, attendanceDate and periodNo are checked against the effective timetable via the TimetableReferenceClient, Then the session is created only if the slot is valid and effective, otherwise the request is rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_INVALID_TIMETABLE (422). Given ACD-05 is unavailable, When a new session is requested, Then it fails closed (503 dependency unavailable) and no unvalidated session is created (FR-02, DDD sections 11 and 56).

Summary: Reject duplicate sessions for the same batch, subject, date and period
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want to enforce one session per batch, subject, date and period, so that duplicate attendance sheets can never exist.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a session already exists for the same tenantId+batchId+subjectId+attendanceDate+periodNo, When another create request arrives, Then it is rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_DUPLICATE_SESSION (409), and two concurrent creates result in exactly one session because the unique compound index enforces the rule at the data layer (FR-05, DDD section 34).

Summary: Update an open attendance session
Description: As an Academic Admin or Faculty member, I want to update the details of a session while it is still open, so that administrative corrections to the session itself are possible before submission.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a session is in status OPEN and I am authorized for its scope, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/attendance/sessions/{id} with the changed fields and the current version, Then the session is updated with optimistic concurrency, and once the session is LOCKED the same call is rejected because post-lock state is immutable (DDD sections 22 and 34).

Summary: View and list attendance sessions
Description: As an authorized user, I want to retrieve a session by id and list sessions filtered by batch, date and status, so that I can find and review attendance sheets.
Acceptance Criteria: Given sessions exist, When I request a session by sessionId or list sessions with filters, Then results are role-scoped, paginated and served from tenant-aware indexes (batch/date, status/date) within the indexed-read P95 target. NOTE: the DDD REST catalog (section 22) lists only create, record, update, student view and report; the get-by-id and list endpoints appear only in the architecture diagram API panel and should be added to the approved contract.

Summary: Cancel an attendance session without deleting evidence
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to cancel a session raised in error, so that it is voided while its records remain available for audit and reporting.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a session was created in error, When an authorized user cancels it, Then the status becomes CANCELLED (terminal, void), the session and any records are retained for audit rather than hard-deleted, and summaries are recalculated excluding it (DDD section 13; diagram rule 'Soft delete - retain records for audit and reporting'). NOTE: CANCELLED exists in the DDD lifecycle, but no cancel endpoint is in the DDD catalog; the diagram shows DELETE /attendance/sessions/{id} (soft).

Summary: Attendance Marking & Roster Validation
Description: Record per-student attendance outcomes against a session with roster-membership, status and duplicate validation. Satisfies FR-03, FR-04, FR-05, FR-06 and DDD sections 24, 35 and 36.

Summary: Mark attendance for a session
Description: As a Faculty member, I want to submit attendance for my session's roster (single student or the whole sheet), so that each student's outcome is recorded once and downstream services are informed.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an OPEN session and an expected roster, When I POST /api/v1/academics/attendance/sessions/{id}/records with records[] (studentId, status) and submittedBy, Then the submission is validated against the expected roster, all records and the session counts are persisted atomically, the summary is recalculated and shortage evaluated, an AttendanceMarked event is written to the outbox, and the response reports the counts (FR-04, FR-06, DDD sections 20, 24 and 65).

Summary: Validate that every student belongs to the session's batch roster
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want to reject attendance for students who are not in the session's batch, so that outcomes can never be attached to the wrong cohort.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a submission contains a studentId not in the resolved roster, When it is validated, Then the whole submission is rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_STUDENT_NOT_IN_BATCH (422) and nothing is persisted (atomic per FR-06). Given the roster source is unavailable, Then unvalidated writes are rejected rather than accepted (DDD sections 11 and 56).

Summary: Validate attendance status against the configured status catalog
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want to accept only statuses defined in the configured catalog (Present, Absent, Leave or configured equivalents), so that summaries always calculate on known outcomes.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a submitted status, When it is checked against the institution's configured status catalog, Then unknown codes are rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_INVALID_STATUS (422), and an optional statusReason is stored for special statuses (DDD sections 11 and 36). NOTE: the DDD defines P/A/L with L meaning Leave and per-session leaveCount, while the diagram domain model shows P/A/L/E and its sample response reports lateCount. The meaning of L (Leave vs Late) and of E must be fixed in the status catalog before build, and the catalog must state how each status counts toward attendance percentage.

Summary: Prevent duplicate attendance records for a student in a session
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want one record per student per session, so that re-submission cannot silently create conflicting outcomes.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a record already exists for tenantId+sessionId+studentId, When another mark is submitted for the same student, Then it is rejected with a 409 conflict and the change must go through the correction path instead (unique index tenant+session+student, DDD Appendix D; diagram rule 'No duplicate attendance for same student/session').

Summary: Enforce the configured marking time window
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want attendance to be markable only within a configured time window around the session, so that back-dated or premature marking is controlled.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a session has a start and end time, When attendance is submitted outside the configured marking window, Then it is rejected with a business-rule error unless the late-entry rule permits it. NOTE: 'Attendance allowed only within configured time window' appears only in the diagram Key Business Rules. The DDD has a SessionWindow (start < end) but no marking-window rule; the window length, its configuration source and the error code must be defined before implementation.

Summary: Exclude holidays and academic events from attendance
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want sessions and marking on holidays or academic-event days to be rejected or flagged using the academic calendar, so that attendance is never recorded on non-teaching days.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the academic calendar marks a date as a holiday or event day, When a session is created or attendance marked for that date, Then the action is rejected or flagged per policy and excluded from percentage calculations (diagram rules 'Holidays and academic events exclude attendance' and 'Real-time validation with academic calendar'). NOTE: the DDD lists ACD-07 Calendar only 'where applicable' (section 61); confirm whether the calendar is a hard dependency and whether a calendar outage fails closed.

Summary: Record capture source and actor on every attendance record
Description: As a Compliance Officer, I want each record to carry who marked it, when, and through which channel, so that the origin of every outcome is traceable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a record is persisted, When it is written, Then markedBy, markedAt, source (FACULTY, MOBILE, BULK, IMPORT or SYSTEM), recordVersion and schemaVersion are stored (DDD Appendix C). NOTE: no BIOMETRIC or RFID source value exists in the DDD; see the Bulk Import & Device Integration epic.

Summary: Support very large rosters with partitioned attendance records
Description: As a Platform Architect, I want records embedded for bounded rosters but stored in a separate or partitioned form for very large rosters or high-concurrency sessions, so that sessions never exceed document limits or hot-spot writes.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a roster below the configured bound, When attendance is stored, Then records are embedded with the session; Given a roster above the bound or high write concurrency, Then records are stored in the separate/partitioned representation while preserving the unique session+student rule and the same read contract (ADR-ACD06-002, DDD sections 32, 35 and 58). The bound value must be a configuration decision validated by load testing.

Summary: Attendance Corrections & Audit Trail
Description: Change recorded attendance only through audited, permissioned corrections that preserve prior values. Satisfies FR-07 and DDD sections 21, 37, 38 and 66. Includes the diagram's correction-approval workflow, which conflicts with the DDD and is flagged for decision.

Summary: Correct an attendance record with a mandatory reason
Description: As an authorized Faculty member or Academic Admin, I want to correct a student's recorded status with a reason, so that mistakes are fixed without losing what was originally recorded.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a marked session and a correction request with studentId, newStatus, reason and expectedVersion, When the policy check passes, Then the record is updated and an attendance_corrections entry is appended in the same transaction, the session moves to CORRECTED, the summary is recalculated, and an AttendanceCorrected event is emitted (FR-07, DDD sections 21, 25 and 66). NOTE: the DDD catalog has no dedicated correction endpoint (PUT sessions/{id} is the nearest); the diagram uses PUT /attendance/records/{id} and /attendance/corrections. The endpoint shape must be confirmed.

Summary: Enforce correction authorization scope
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want corrections limited to authorized Faculty within correction policy and to Academic Admin, so that unauthorized changes to attendance truth are impossible.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a caller without correction rights for the session's scope, When a correction is attempted, Then it is rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_CORRECTION_FORBIDDEN (403) and the attempt is audited (DDD sections 50, 51 and 56).

Summary: Keep an immutable, append-only correction trail
Description: As an Auditor, I want every correction stored as an append-only entry with old value, new value, reason, actor and versions, so that the full change history can be reconstructed at any time.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a correction is applied, When the entry is written, Then it captures oldStatus, newStatus, reason, correctedBy, correctedAt, authorizationScope, previousVersion, newVersion and correlationId, can never be updated or deleted, is access-restricted, is retrievable by session and student, and is retained longer than operational data (DDD sections 37, 38 and 51; ADR-ACD06-003).

Summary: Reject stale corrections using the expected version
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want corrections to carry the record version they were based on, so that two people cannot overwrite each other's corrections.
Acceptance Criteria: Given expectedVersion does not match the current recordVersion, When the correction is submitted, Then it is rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_VERSION_CONFLICT (409) and nothing changes (DDD sections 25 and 53; ADR-ACD06-006).

Summary: Support configurable late-entry corrections
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to configure how long after a session faculty may correct their own attendance, so that routine late fixes do not require administrative escalation.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a configured late-entry period, When a Faculty member corrects within the period, Then the correction proceeds under the normal audited path; after the period it requires the higher authorization scope (diagram rule 'Support late entry corrections (configurable)'). NOTE: not defined in the DDD; the period, its configuration source and the role that can override are open decisions.

Summary: Route corrections through an approval workflow (decision required)
Description: As a Department Head or Academic Admin approver, I want corrections to be reviewed before they take effect, so that changes to attendance truth carry a second sign-off.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the approval workflow is adopted, When a correction is requested, Then it is held as pending, AttendanceCorrectionRequested is emitted, and only on approval is the record changed and the correction appended, with AttendanceCorrectionApproved or AttendanceCorrectionRejected emitted and the rejection reason retained (diagram rule 'Corrections require approval (HOD/Admin)', API panel and events panel). NOTE: this conflicts with the DDD, where a correction is applied directly by an authorized actor with a mandatory reason. Three decisions are needed first: (1) does approval replace or supplement the direct path, (2) which role approves (the diagram says HOD/Admin), and (3) does the workflow run locally or through the College Admin Module's Approvals & Workflow capability, as was decided for ACD-04 split/merge. If routed through ADM02, a matching workflow-type story is needed in the ADM02 backlog.

Summary: Attendance Session Lifecycle Governance
Description: Govern the session state machine DRAFT, OPEN, SUBMITTED, LOCKED, CORRECTED, ARCHIVED with CANCELLED as a terminal void state, without deleting evidence. Satisfies DDD sections 13 and 34 and the audit rules in section 51.

Summary: Submit an attendance session
Description: As a Faculty member, I want to submit a completed session, so that my attendance sheet is formally handed over as final.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a session is OPEN with attendance recorded, When I submit it, Then the status becomes SUBMITTED and the submission is audited (DDD sections 13 and 51). NOTE: the DDD does not say whether unmarked roster members block submission or default to a status; confirm the rule.

Summary: Lock a submitted session
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want a submitted session to be locked, so that its records can only change through audited corrections.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a session is SUBMITTED, When it is locked, Then the status becomes LOCKED, direct edits to the session and records are rejected, and only the correction path can change outcomes (DDD section 34 'immutable post-lock semantics'; audit of lock per section 51).

Summary: Archive completed sessions
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want old locked or corrected sessions archived, so that they leave operational queries while remaining available for audit.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a session is LOCKED or CORRECTED and past its operational window, When it is archived, Then the status becomes ARCHIVED, the archive is audited, records stay retained under the retention policy, and summaries remain valid (DDD sections 13, 51 and 60).

Summary: Reject invalid lifecycle transitions
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want every transition validated against the state machine, so that a session can never skip or reverse states illegally.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a requested transition is not allowed from the current status (for example OPEN directly to LOCKED, or any change from CANCELLED), When it is invoked, Then it is rejected with a 409 state-conflict error and the status is unchanged. NOTE: the DDD error taxonomy (section 53) has no invalid-transition code; one must be added.

Summary: Close sessions at end of day
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want open sessions closed automatically at the end of the day, so that attendance cannot stay editable indefinitely.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a configured end-of-day cut-off, When it passes, Then remaining OPEN or SUBMITTED sessions are closed per policy, an AttendanceSessionClosed event is emitted and the action is audited (diagram workflow step 'Close Session (End of Day)' and events panel). NOTE: the DDD has the LOCKED state but no trigger or timing for it; the cut-off, grace period and whether close means SUBMITTED or LOCKED must be defined.

Summary: Attendance Summaries & Percentage Calculation
Description: Maintain derived, read-optimized attendance summaries per student, subject and term that can always be rebuilt from authoritative records. Satisfies FR-08 and DDD sections 39, 40, 46 and ADR-ACD06-005.

Summary: Recalculate the summary on every accepted mark or correction
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want the affected student's summary recalculated whenever attendance is accepted or corrected, so that percentages reflect current truth.
Acceptance Criteria: Given attendance is marked or corrected, When the change is accepted, Then the summary for tenantId+studentId+subjectId+termId is created or updated with totalSessions, presentCount, absentCount, leaveCount, attendancePercentage, calculatedAt and sourceVersion, with a unique index guaranteeing one summary per key (FR-08, DDD sections 39, 40 and 46).

Summary: Calculate attendance percentage under the academic rules
Description: As a Student or Academic Admin, I want percentages computed consistently under institutional rules, so that shortage decisions are fair and reproducible.
Acceptance Criteria: Given accepted records for a student, subject and term, When the percentage is aggregated, Then it is derived from eligible sessions and Present outcomes, excluding cancelled sessions and excluded holiday or event days (DDD section 46; diagram rule 'Attendance percentage calculated as per academic rules'). NOTE: the DDD does not say whether Leave, Late or on-duty statuses count as present or are removed from the denominator; the rule must be specified per status.

Summary: Rebuild summaries and reconcile drift
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want summaries rebuildable from authoritative records and periodically reconciled, so that any drift or lost update is detected and repaired.
Acceptance Criteria: Given summaries are derived data, When a rebuild or the periodic reconciliation runs, Then each summary is recomputed from attendance_records, drift is corrected and reported, and shortage state is re-evaluated (DDD sections 40 and 47).

Summary: Expose summary freshness and support asynchronous materialization at scale
Description: As a Platform Architect, I want summary updates to run inline for bounded workloads and asynchronously at high scale, with freshness visible to readers, so that marking latency stays low without hiding lag.
Acceptance Criteria: Given high marking volume, When summary materialization is asynchronous, Then calculatedAt is exposed where permitted, reconciliation closes any gap, and marking latency targets are met (DDD sections 55 and 56).

Summary: View attendance summaries by student, batch and subject
Description: As an authorized user, I want summary views per student, per batch and per subject, so that I can review attendance standing at the level I manage.
Acceptance Criteria: Given summaries exist, When I request a student, batch or subject summary, Then results are role-scoped and served from the student/date, batch/shortage and subject/percentage indexes (DDD section 40). NOTE: the DDD catalog exposes only the student view and the report endpoint; the diagram adds /summary, /summary/student, /summary/batch and /summary/subject.

Summary: Shortage Detection
Description: Detect students whose attendance falls below the configured minimum and raise a single reliable signal. Satisfies FR-09 and DDD section 47.

Summary: Evaluate shortage against the configured minimum threshold
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want each summary evaluated against the applicable minimum attendance threshold after every accepted mark or correction and during reconciliation, so that shortage status is always current.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a summary changes or reconciliation runs, When the ShortageRuleEngine evaluates it, Then shortageFlag and shortageThreshold are set from the configured minimum (FR-09, DDD sections 39 and 47).

Summary: Emit AttendanceShortageDetected only on a false-to-true transition
Description: As a downstream consumer (Notification, Analytics), I want one shortage event per crossing, so that students and staff are not flooded with duplicate alerts.
Acceptance Criteria: Given shortageFlag was false, When an evaluation sets it true, Then exactly one AttendanceShortageDetected event is written to the outbox; repeated evaluations while the flag stays true emit nothing (DDD section 47). NOTE: the DDD publishes this event but it is absent from the diagram events panel; keep the DDD behaviour.

Summary: Resolve the applicable threshold from its authoritative source
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want a defined source of truth and precedence for the minimum attendance threshold, so that shortage flags are consistent with institutional and course rules.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a threshold is needed for a student, subject and term, When it is resolved, Then it comes from the agreed policy source with a defined precedence between institutional default and course-level rule. NOTE: the DDD says thresholds are 'configured' with Shared Configuration as an upstream dependency (section 61), while the ACD-01 design owns per-course attendance rules in course_attendance_policy. Decide which is authoritative, whether course-level overrides institution-level, and how ACD-06 reads it.

Summary: Query shortage lists for a batch
Description: As a Department Head or Faculty member, I want the list of students in shortage for a batch, so that I can act on them.
Acceptance Criteria: Given shortage flags are maintained, When I request a batch shortage list, Then results are returned from the batch+shortageFlag index, scoped to my authorization (DDD sections 40 and 45).

Summary: Attendance Reporting & Export
Description: Provide student history views, paginated reports and controlled exports. Satisfies FR-12 and DDD sections 22, 45 and 58.

Summary: View a student's attendance history
Description: As a Student, Parent or Academic Admin, I want to see a student's attendance history, so that attendance standing is transparent to those entitled to see it.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a student has attendance data, When GET /api/v1/academics/attendance/student/{studentId} is called, Then a paginated history is returned only where I am the student, the linked parent or an authorized admin, with summary freshness shown where allowed (DDD sections 22, 45 and 50).

Summary: Generate paginated attendance reports
Description: As a Faculty member or Academic Admin, I want reports filtered by date range, batch and subject (daily, weekly, monthly), so that I can review attendance across my scope.
Acceptance Criteria: Given report filters, When GET /api/v1/academics/attendance/report is called, Then results are paginated, Faculty see only their scope while Admin sees the whole institution, and indexed reports meet P95 < 2 seconds (FR-12, DDD sections 50 and 57; diagram responsibility 'Generate daily, weekly, monthly attendance reports').

Summary: Export attendance reports with export controls
Description: As an authorized user, I want to export reports to PDF or Excel under export controls, so that attendance data can leave the platform only in an audited, permitted way.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I hold export permission, When I request an export, Then the file respects my role's field visibility and masking, the export is audited, and an AttendanceExported event is emitted (DDD sections 49 and 51; diagram export endpoint and events panel). NOTE: the export endpoint and event are diagram-only; the DDD requires export audit and controls but defines no endpoint.

Summary: Run heavy reports asynchronously
Description: As a Platform Architect, I want large reports produced by asynchronous jobs, so that reporting load never breaches normal API latency targets.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a report exceeds the synchronous size threshold, When it is requested, Then it is processed as an asynchronous job and retrieved on completion, while normal API P95 stays under 300 ms (DDD section 58).

Summary: Bulk Import & Device Integration
Description: Accept attendance from bulk files, biometric/RFID devices and external LMS integrations. The DDD data dictionary allows source values BULK, IMPORT and MOBILE, but the DDD defines no import endpoint, no device integration and no LMS sync; these come from the architecture diagram (Capture Modes panel, Import endpoint, Devices and LMS rows) and are flagged for architectural confirmation.

Summary: Bulk import attendance from CSV or Excel
Description: As an authorized Academic Admin, I want to import attendance from a file, so that sheets captured offline can be loaded in one operation.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a well-formed CSV or Excel file and import permission, When I POST /api/v1/academics/attendance/import, Then each row passes the same session, roster and status validation as normal marking, rows are stored with source IMPORT or BULK, and the response reports per-row errors, returning 207 partial success where some rows fail (diagram Import endpoint, failure panel and rule 'Bulk import allowed only for authorized users'). NOTE: not in the DDD catalog. Also decide whether partial success is compatible with FR-06 atomic persistence (atomic per session versus per row).

Summary: Ingest attendance from biometric and RFID devices
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want device-captured attendance mapped into sessions, so that automated capture replaces manual sheets where devices exist.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a registered device submits attendance through the API/SDK, When the event is received, Then it is authenticated, mapped to a student and to the correct timetable session, validated like manual marking and stored with a device source, and device-integration failures return 503 without losing buffered data (diagram Capture Modes, Integration and Failure panels). NOTE: absent from the DDD, whose source enum has no BIOMETRIC or RFID. Open decisions: device identity and enrolment, student mapping, offline buffering and replay, and duplicate handling versus manual marks.

Summary: Provide attendance to the external LMS
Description: As an LMS integrator, I want attendance data available to the LMS, so that learning-platform records stay aligned with authoritative attendance.
Acceptance Criteria: Given attendance is marked or corrected, When the LMS needs it, Then it receives the data through published events (DDD downstream consumers, section 62). NOTE: the diagram shows a REST sync to an external LMS while the DDD treats LMS as an event consumer; confirm whether a REST pull or push endpoint is required at all.

Summary: Event-Driven Integration
Description: Publish attendance events reliably through a transactional outbox and consume timetable, student and batch events, so LMS, CAM, ACD-10 and Notification stay eventually consistent without shared databases. Satisfies FR-10 and DDD sections 27 to 31.

Summary: Publish attendance events via the transactional outbox
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want AttendanceSessionCreated, AttendanceMarked, AttendanceCorrected and AttendanceShortageDetected written to an outbox in the same transaction as the change, so that no event is lost when the broker is down.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a create, mark, correction or shortage transition commits, When the transaction completes, Then the event is recorded in outbox_events with the canonical envelope (eventId, eventType, source, occurredAt, entityType, entityId, version, correlationId, data), correlation and causation IDs are preserved, and a publisher retries until acknowledged (FR-10, DDD sections 30, 31 and 41). NOTE: the diagram lists further events (AttendanceUpdated, AttendanceCorrectionRequested/Approved/Rejected, AttendanceSummaryGenerated, AttendanceSessionClosed, AttendanceExported); these are emitted only if the matching features are adopted.

Summary: Consume TimetablePublished to establish timetable context
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want to consume TimetablePublished from ACD-05, so that session validation uses the currently effective timetable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a TimetablePublished event is received, When it is processed, Then the effective timetable context used by session validation is updated (DDD section 29).

Summary: Consume TimetableChanged and TimetableSuperseded (alignment needed)
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want to react when a published timetable is changed or superseded, so that I never validate new sessions against a replaced timetable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given ACD-05 publishes a new effective version, When the corresponding event is received, Then new sessions validate against the new version while existing sessions keep their original timetableEntryId as history. NOTE: the DDD consumes only TimetablePublished, but ACD-05 also emits TimetableChanged and TimetableSuperseded for mid-term changes, and its design does not say whether TimetablePublished also fires for a new version. If it does not, ACD-06 would keep validating against the old timetable. Align the contract with ACD-05 before build.

Summary: Consume StudentAddedToBatch to refresh roster context
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want roster context refreshed when a student joins a batch, so that new members are eligible for later sessions.
Acceptance Criteria: Given StudentAddedToBatch is received, When it is processed, Then the roster context used for future sessions includes the student from the event's effective date and already-recorded sessions are not rewritten (DDD section 29). NOTE: the ACD-04 diagram names this event StudentEnrolledInBatch; the DDDs use StudentAddedToBatch.

Summary: Consume StudentStatusChanged to update eligibility
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want student eligibility updated when a student's status changes, so that ineligible students are not marked in future sessions.
Acceptance Criteria: Given StudentStatusChanged is received, When it is processed, Then future rosters reflect the new eligibility while historical attendance truth is preserved unchanged (DDD section 29).

Summary: Deduplicate inbound events by eventId
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want each inbound event processed once, so that redelivery never causes duplicate effects.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an event with an already-processed eventId is redelivered, When it arrives, Then it is recognised and skipped without error (DDD section 31).

Summary: Route poison events to a dead-letter queue with controlled replay
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want repeatedly failing events parked in a dead-letter store, so that they can be investigated and replayed without blocking the stream.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an event fails after the configured retries, When retries are exhausted, Then it is stored in dead_letter_events with failureCode, failureReason, attemptCount and timestamps, an alert is raised, and it can be replayed under control (DDD sections 43 and 56).

Summary: Consume BatchSplit and BatchMerged to keep attendance continuity (dependency gap)
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want to consume batch split and merge events with their student reassignment map, so that current rosters, open sessions and batch-keyed summaries follow students to their new batch while history stays intact.
Acceptance Criteria: Given ACD-04 publishes BatchSplit or BatchMerged with a per-student old-to-new batch map, When it is processed, Then future sessions resolve rosters from the new batches, open sessions on affected batches are handled per policy, historical sessions and records keep their original batchId, and each student's summary continues under the same student+subject+term key with its batchId updated. NOTE: split/merge is itself unspecified in the ACD-04 DDD and this event is not in the ACD-06 DDD's consumed list; this story records the dependency and needs sign-off from both service owners.

Summary: Idempotency, Concurrency & Transaction Integrity
Description: Make writes safe to retry and safe under concurrency. Satisfies FR-06, FR-11 and DDD sections 44, 54, 55 and ADR-ACD06-006.

Summary: Support idempotent create, mark and correct requests
Description: As an API client, I want to send an Idempotency-Key on retryable writes, so that a retried request never creates a duplicate session, record or correction.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a request is retried with the same tenantId+idempotencyKey and the same request hash, When it is reprocessed, Then the stored response is returned without re-executing the write; the same key with a different hash is rejected as a conflict; records expire through the TTL on expiresAt (FR-11, DDD sections 42 and 54).

Summary: Apply optimistic concurrency to sessions and records
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want version checks on sessions and records, so that concurrent edits cannot silently overwrite each other.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a write is based on a stale session version or recordVersion, When it is applied, Then it is rejected with ACD_ATTENDANCE_VERSION_CONFLICT (409) (DDD sections 34, 44 and 53).

Summary: Commit session, records and outbox atomically
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want attendance changes and their outbox entries committed together, so that state and events can never diverge.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a mark or correction touches sessions, records, corrections and outbox_events, When it executes, Then all writes commit atomically where the topology supports transactions, otherwise the outbox pattern guarantees eventual publication; summary materialization may be transactional for bounded workloads or asynchronous with reconciliation (FR-06, DDD sections 44 and 55).

Summary: Security, RBAC & Audit Governance
Description: Enforce role and attribute based access, tenant isolation, classification and a complete audit trail. Satisfies DDD sections 48 to 51 and the diagram RBAC panel (which adds Department Head, Exam Cell and External API roles).

Summary: Enforce the API authorization matrix
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want every endpoint to check role and scope before any business logic, so that each actor can do only what the matrix allows.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a caller, When a request arrives, Then Super Admin has all rights, Academic Admin administers within the institution, Faculty creates and marks within assignment, Student holds ATTENDANCE_VIEW_SELF, Parent holds ATTENDANCE_VIEW_LINKED_STUDENT, Management reads authorized aggregates, and anything else is rejected with 403 (DDD sections 48 and 50).

Summary: Limit Faculty to their assigned batches and subjects
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want Faculty able to create and mark attendance only for assigned batch and subject combinations, so that staff cannot record attendance for classes they do not teach.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a Faculty caller, When they create or mark a session, Then the batch/subject assignment is verified and violations are rejected and audited (DDD section 48; diagram rule 'Faculty can mark attendance only for assigned subjects/batches'). NOTE: the DDD does not name the assignment source (the ACD-05 timetable entry's faculty, or HRM); confirm it.

Summary: Let Students view only their own attendance
Description: As a Student, I want to see my own attendance and no one else's, so that my data stays private.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I hold ATTENDANCE_VIEW_SELF, When I request attendance, Then only my records and summaries are returned and any other studentId returns 403 (DDD sections 48 and 50).

Summary: Let Parents view their linked student's attendance
Description: As a Parent, I want read-only access to my linked student's attendance, so that I can follow their progress without any write ability.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I hold ATTENDANCE_VIEW_LINKED_STUDENT, When I request attendance, Then only students linked to me are returned, read-only, based on the linkage authority in Student Management, and nothing about other students is exposed (DDD section 50).

Summary: Let Department Heads view department attendance
Description: As a Department Head, I want to see attendance for my department, so that I can monitor and follow up.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am a Department Head, When I request attendance, Then results are limited to my department's batches and subjects (diagram RBAC panel). NOTE: this role is not in the DDD authorization matrix.

Summary: Give the Exam Cell consolidated read access
Description: As an Exam Cell member, I want consolidated attendance reports, so that I can work from institution-approved attendance data.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am Exam Cell, When I request consolidated reports, Then I receive read-only results within my scope (diagram RBAC panel). NOTE: this role is not in the DDD matrix and the intended use (for example exam eligibility) is unspecified.

Summary: Give External API consumers scoped read-only access
Description: As an external integrator, I want read-only access limited to my key's scope, so that I can consume attendance without write access.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I authenticate as an External API client, When I call an attendance endpoint, Then only data within my granted scope is returned and any write is rejected (diagram RBAC panel). NOTE: not in the DDD matrix.

Summary: Guarantee tenant isolation on every query
Description: As a Security Architect, I want tenantId enforced on every read and write, so that one institution can never see another's attendance.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any request, When data is queried or written, Then tenantId scoping is applied through tenant-aware compound indexes, cross-tenant access is impossible, and this is proven by security tests before release (DDD sections 45, 49 and 68).

Summary: Audit every material attendance event
Description: As a Compliance Officer, I want session creation, submission, lock, correction, archive, export and authorization failures audited, so that any action is attributable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any listed event occurs, When it is processed, Then an audit entry records actor, requestId, correlationId and timestamp, and for corrections the old value, new value and reason (DDD section 51).

Summary: Classify, encrypt and protect attendance data
Description: As a Security Architect, I want attendance treated as internal or confidential data with encryption and export controls, so that it is protected in transit, at rest and in backups.
Acceptance Criteria: Given attendance data, When it is stored or transmitted, Then TLS 1.2+ is enforced, encryption at rest and encrypted backups are enabled, secrets are centrally managed, projections are restricted by role and exports are controlled (DDD section 49).

Summary: Observability, Reliability & Performance
Description: Provide telemetry, alerting, defined failure behaviour, performance targets, scale, disaster recovery and retention. Satisfies DDD sections 52, 54, 56 to 60.

Summary: Emit structured logs, metrics and traces
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want structured logs with request and correlation IDs plus metrics and distributed tracing, so that any request can be followed end to end.
Acceptance Criteria: Given production traffic, When requests complete, Then logs, API latency and error metrics, DB metrics, outbox lag, broker and consumer lag, session and record volume and shortage counts are available and a trace spans Gateway to consumers (DDD section 52).

Summary: Alert on reliability and drift signals
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want alerts on error rate, latency, outbox lag, consumer lag, DLQ growth and summary drift, so that problems are caught early.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a monitored signal breaches its threshold for the alert window, When detected, Then an alert with triage context reaches the on-call channel (DDD sections 52 and 56).

Summary: Define behaviour under dependency outages
Description: As a Platform Architect, I want explicit outage behaviour, so that failures degrade safely instead of corrupting attendance truth.
Acceptance Criteria: Given each outage, Then a timetable outage fails closed for new sessions, a roster outage rejects unvalidated writes, a broker outage falls back to the outbox, summary lag exposes freshness, an unauthorized correction is rejected and audited, and a poison event is retried then sent to the DLQ (DDD section 56).

Summary: Apply bounded exponential backoff to transient failures
Description: As the Attendance Management Service, I want transient dependency and broker failures retried with bounded backoff, so that brief faults self-heal.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a transient failure, When retried, Then backoff is exponential and bounded, and deterministic domain failures are never retried (DDD section 54).

Summary: Meet latency and high-volume marking targets
Description: As a Platform Architect, I want the service to meet its latency targets under high-volume marking, so that peak periods do not degrade the experience.
Acceptance Criteria: Given production-representative load, When exercised, Then availability is at least 99.9 percent, normal API P95 is under 300 ms, indexed search and report P95 is under 2 seconds and create or update is under 500 ms excluding async consumers, verified by performance tests (DDD sections 57 and 67).

Summary: Scale horizontally with tenant-aware partitioning
Description: As a Platform Architect, I want stateless pods, bounded bulk writes and broker partitioning by tenant and session, so that growth needs no redesign.
Acceptance Criteria: Given rising load, When autoscaling triggers, Then capacity grows without interruption, bulk writes stay bounded, events are partitioned by tenant and session, and Redis may cache stable reference data (DDD section 58).

Summary: Recover from disaster with post-restore reconciliation
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want encrypted backups, point-in-time recovery and regular restore drills, so that RPO and RTO are met and derived data is trustworthy after recovery.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the backup schedule, When a restore drill runs, Then the data is complete, correction history is intact, the outbox is recovered and summaries are reconciled from records afterwards (DDD section 59).

Summary: Enforce data retention rules
Description: As a Compliance Officer, I want retention applied per data type, so that evidence is kept as long as required and no longer than needed.
Acceptance Criteria: Given each data type, Then records follow institutional and legal retention with soft delete only, corrections and audit are long-lived, summaries remain for the reporting horizon and are rebuildable, outbox rows stay until published and DLQ rows through incident closure (DDD section 60; diagram rule 'Soft delete - retain records for audit and reporting').

Summary: API Standards, Error Handling & Contracts
Description: Deliver a consistent, versioned REST contract with the standard envelope and the documented error taxonomy. Cross-cutting.

Summary: Publish and version the attendance API contract
Description: As an API consumer, I want an approved, versioned OpenAPI specification, so that I can integrate against a stable contract.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the service, When the contract is published, Then it covers the DDD catalog (create session, record attendance, update session, student view, report) and breaking changes require a new version (DDD sections 22 and 68). NOTE: the diagram lists roughly eighteen endpoints (sessions list and get, cancel, mark, import, records, corrections, summaries, export); the approved contract must state which are in scope.

Summary: Return the standard envelope with pagination, filtering and sorting
Description: As an API consumer, I want uniform responses and list semantics, so that clients handle every endpoint the same way.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any call under /api/v1, When it returns, Then it uses the standard envelope with requestId and correlationId and supports standardized pagination, filtering and sorting (DDD section 26).

Summary: Map every failure to its documented error code and status
Description: As an API consumer, I want each failure mapped to a stable code and HTTP status, so that client error handling is reliable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given each failure, Then the API returns ACD_ATTENDANCE_INVALID_TIMETABLE 422, ACD_ATTENDANCE_STUDENT_NOT_IN_BATCH 422, ACD_ATTENDANCE_INVALID_STATUS 422, ACD_ATTENDANCE_DUPLICATE_SESSION 409, ACD_ATTENDANCE_CORRECTION_FORBIDDEN 403, ACD_ATTENDANCE_VERSION_CONFLICT 409 and 503 for unavailable dependencies (DDD section 53). NOTE: the diagram Failure Handling panel uses 400 for validation errors where the DDD uses 422; follow the DDD unless the architecture board decides otherwise. The diagram's 207 partial success applies only if bulk import is adopted, and 'session closed' has no DDD code yet.

Summary: Attendance Intelligence & Analytics (Advisory)
Description: Feed attendance facts to analytics and provide advisory insights without ever altering attendance truth. Satisfies DDD sections 62 and 64.

Summary: Publish attendance facts to Analytics and downstream consumers
Description: As ACD-10 Analytics, I want attendance data delivered by events and the data lake, so that reporting and models use authoritative attendance.
Acceptance Criteria: Given attendance is marked, corrected or summarised, When events are published, Then LMS, CAM, ACD-10, Notification and the reporting warehouse can consume them through versioned contracts without direct database access (DDD sections 62 and 63).

Summary: Provide early shortage-risk and marking-anomaly signals
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want trends, early shortage risk, marking anomalies, batch volatility and correction-frequency signals, so that I can intervene before problems escalate.
Acceptance Criteria: Given accumulated attendance history, When the analytics layer runs, Then it produces advisory indicators including correlation with timetable and calendar changes, clearly labelled as advisory (DDD section 64).

Summary: Guarantee intelligence cannot silently mutate attendance truth
Description: As a Compliance Officer, I want analytics and AI outputs unable to change attendance records, so that recorded truth is only ever changed through validated, audited paths.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any intelligence component, When it proposes a change, Then it can only do so through the service's own validated APIs under a human-authorized correction, and any such action is audited (DDD section 64).

Summary: End-to-End Scenarios & Cross-Module Integration
Description: Prove complete flows and every cross-module contract before release. Satisfies DDD sections 65 to 68 and the diagram Cross-Module Integration panel.

Summary: E2E: create, mark, summarise, detect shortage, correct and report
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test of the full attendance lifecycle, so that the designed flow is proven to work together.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a valid timetable slot and roster, When a session is created, attendance marked, the summary and shortage evaluated, a correction applied and a report generated, Then every step succeeds, the expected events are observed and the report matches the corrected data (DDD sections 65, 66 and 67).

Summary: E2E: a correction preserves history and recomputes derived state
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want a test proving corrections keep the prior value and update summaries and shortage correctly, so that the audit and calculation guarantees hold.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a marked session, When an authorized correction is applied, Then the previous value is retained in the correction trail, the summary and shortage flag are recalculated, a single shortage event is emitted on a new crossing, and a stale correction is rejected with 409 (DDD sections 47 and 66).

Summary: E2E: rejection paths
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want tests for every documented rejection, so that error behaviour is verified against the taxonomy.
Acceptance Criteria: Given each invalid input (unscheduled slot, student not in batch, unknown status, duplicate session, unauthorized correction, stale version), When submitted, Then the documented code and status are returned and nothing is persisted (DDD section 53).

Summary: E2E: mid-term timetable change does not corrupt attendance
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want a test where the timetable is superseded mid-term, so that new sessions validate against the new version while old sessions stay intact.
Acceptance Criteria: Given existing sessions and a superseded timetable, When ACD-05 publishes a replacement, Then new sessions use the new timetable, old sessions and summaries are unchanged, and the ACD-05 event contract is confirmed to reach ACD-06 (see the timetable-change consumption story).

Summary: E2E: batch split or merge preserves each student's attendance continuity
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want a test that splits or merges a batch mid-term, so that students keep a continuous attendance record under their new batch.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch with sessions and summaries, When ACD-04 executes an approved split or merge, Then new sessions resolve the new rosters, history keeps its original batchId and each student's summary continues under the same key. NOTE: depends on the unspecified ACD-04 split/merge design.

Summary: Validate integrations before production sign-off
Description: As a Release Manager, I want contract and integration tests against every module in the integration table, so that ACD-06 is not released until its dependencies are proven.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the release candidate, When the suite runs against ACD-01 (course details), ACD-03 (subject existence), ACD-04 (batch and section), ACD-05 (timetable session validation), HRM (faculty details), STM (student details), the academic calendar, COM (notifications), ACD-10 (analytics), the LMS and any devices, Then all REST and event contracts pass, and the Production Definition of Done items (approved OpenAPI, tested rules, deployed validators and indexes, working outbox/idempotency/DLQ, reviewed RBAC, verified audit, dashboards and tracing, tested DR, met load targets, registered event contracts, passed tenant isolation) are met (DDD section 68).
